claim: The General Assembly convenes in first regular session on the first Monday of January of the odd-numbered year, and in second regular session on the same date the next year
quote: Each general assembly shall convene in first regular session on the first Monday of January in the odd-numbered year, or on the succeeding day if the first Monday of January is a legal holiday

claim: A law takes effect ninety days after the governor files it with the secretary of state, unless an exception applies
quote: No law passed by the general assembly shall go into effect until ninety days after it shall have been filed by the governor in the office of the secretary of state

claim: County officers are elected in November of even-numbered years and all other elective officers in November of odd-numbered years
quote: Elections for state and county officers shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in even numbered years; and all elections for all other elective officers shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in the odd numbered years.

claim: County officers are elected in even-numbered years
quote: of elective state and county officers, in the even-numbered years

claim: Municipal and township officers and school board members are elected in odd-numbered years
quote: For municipal and township officers, members of boards of education, judges and clerks of municipal courts, in the odd-numbered years

claim: The regular municipal election is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each odd-numbered year
quote: "Regular municipal election" means the election held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in each odd-numbered year.

claim: The primary is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May, except in presidential primary years
quote: Primary elections shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May of each year except in years in which a presidential primary election is held.

claim: In presidential primary years all primaries move to the third Tuesday after the first Monday in March, unless a charter provides otherwise
quote: all primary elections shall be held on the third Tuesday after the first Monday in March except as otherwise authorized by a municipal or county charter

claim: A municipal or county charter may set its own primary day; special elections are otherwise limited to set days
quote: or on the day authorized by a particular municipal or county charter for the holding of a primary election

claim: Special elections on local questions are held on general election day unless a law or charter provides otherwise
quote: No special election shall be held on a day other than the day of a general election, unless a law or charter provides otherwise

claim: At a primary, a voter can be challenged on party affiliation, judged from the party primaries voted in the current and previous two calendar years
quote: Such party affiliation shall be determined by examining the elector's voting record for the current year and the immediately preceding two calendar years

claim: A challenged primary voter may still vote by stating under penalty of election falsification that they wish to affiliate with that party
quote: that the person desires to be affiliated with and supports the principles of the political party whose primary ballot the person desires to vote

claim: Primaries nominate candidates of political parties for the offices voted on at the next general election
quote: for the purpose of nominating persons as candidates of political parties for election to offices to be voted for at the succeeding general election

claim: County offices are among those with party nominations at the primary
quote: Candidates for party nominations to state, district, county, and municipal offices or positions, for which party nominations are provided by law

claim: Townships and municipalities under 2,000 hold no party primaries for their offices unless a majority of electors petition for them
quote: Primary elections shall not be held for the nomination of candidates for election as officers of any township, or any municipal corporation having a population of less than two thousand

claim: In municipalities of 2,000 or more, offices are nominated the same way the place nominated them in 1989 unless voters have since changed it
quote: shall be the same as the manner in which candidates were nominated for election as officers in the municipal corporation in 1989

claim: Voters in a nonpartisan municipality of 2,000 or more can switch to party primaries by referendum
quote: the question of changing to the primary-election method of nominating persons as candidates for election as officers of the municipal corporation

claim: Voters in a partisan township or municipality can switch to nonpartisan nomination and election by referendum
quote: be nominated as candidates by nominating petition and be elected only in a nonpartisan election

claim: Township officers are nominated only by nominating petition unless a majority of electors petition for a primary
quote: Nominations of candidates for election as officers of a township shall be made only by nominating petitions, unless a majority of the electors of such township have petitioned for a primary election.

claim: The nonpartisan ballot carries school board races, municipal and township offices in places without party primaries, and charter-municipality offices on separate ballots
quote: municipal or township offices for municipal corporations and townships in which primary elections are not held for nomination of candidates by political parties, and municipal offices of municipal corporations having charters which provide for separate ballots

claim: School board candidates appear on the nonpartisan ballot
quote: The name of each candidate for member of a city, local, or exempted village board of education shall appear on the nonpartisan ballot.

claim: Educational service center governing board candidates appear on the nonpartisan ballot
quote: The name of each candidate for election as a member of a governing board of an educational service center shall appear on the nonpartisan ballot.

claim: The candidate with the most votes wins; ties are resolved by lot
quote: If more than the number of candidates to be elected to an office received the largest and an equal number of votes, such tie shall be resolved by lot

claim: Ranked choice and instant runoff voting are prohibited except as permitted under the county and municipal home rule articles
quote: Except as otherwise permitted under Article X or Article XVIII, Ohio Constitution, no election shall be conducted in this state using ranked choice voting or instant runoff voting.

claim: An independent candidate is one who claims not to be affiliated with a political party and files a statement of candidacy and nominating petition
quote: "Independent candidate" means any candidate who claims not to be affiliated with a political party

claim: Independent candidates for offices with primaries file a statement of candidacy and nominating petition by the day before the primary
quote: shall file no later than four p.m. of the day before the day of the primary election immediately preceding the general election

claim: Only electors qualified to vote on the candidacy may sign a petition
quote: Only electors qualified to vote on the candidacy or issue which is the subject of the petition shall sign a petition.

claim: A person who sought a party nomination at the primary cannot run as an independent at the following general election, except for school board and township trustee and similar offices
quote: at the following general election for any office other than the office of member of the state board of education

claim: A county board of commissioners has three members
quote: The board of county commissioners shall consist of three persons

claim: Commissioners are elected on a staggered four-year cycle, one in one even year and two in the next
quote: In November, 1974, and quadrennially thereafter, one county commissioner shall be elected

claim: The legislature may provide alternative forms of county government, which take effect only on voter approval
quote: may provide by general law alternative forms of county government. No alternative form shall become operative in any county until submitted to the electors thereof

claim: A county may adopt a charter, and the charter decides which officers are elected and how; elections are not reserved to state law at the county tier
quote: Every such charter shall provide the form of government of the county and shall determine which of its officers shall be elected and the manner of their election

claim: Summit County has a charter with an elected county executive
quote: The County Executive shall be the chief executive officer of the County.

claim: Summit County Council has eleven members nominated and elected as county officers are under general law
quote: It shall consist of eleven (11) members who shall be nominated and elected as provided in this Charter and in the manner provided by general law for County officers.

claim: Cuyahoga County has a charter with an elected county executive, nominated and elected as general law provides for county officers
quote: shall be nominated and elected in the manner provided for county officers by general law and this Charter

claim: Cuyahoga County Council has eleven members elected by district for four-year terms
quote: Beginning with the 2012 general election, the term for each member of Council shall be four years.

claim: The legislature provides by general law for the election of township officers
quote: The General Assembly shall provide by general law for the election of such township officers as may be necessary.

claim: Every township has a board of three trustees on staggered four-year terms
quote: In each township there shall be a board of township trustees consisting of three members.

claim: Municipal corporations are cities (5,000 or more) or villages (all others)
quote: Municipal corporations are hereby classified into cities and villages. All such corporations having a population of five thousand or over shall be cities; all others shall be villages.

claim: Statutory city council has at least seven members, four by ward and three at large, growing with population to at most seventeen
quote: composed of not fewer than seven members, four of whom shall be elected by wards and three of whom shall be elected by electors of the city at large

claim: A city can set council size between five and seventeen by referendum
quote: composed of not fewer than five nor more than seventeen members

claim: Statutory city council members serve two-year terms
quote: Members shall serve for a term of two years commencing on the first day of January next after their election.

claim: A city can change council terms from two to four years by referendum
quote: the question of whether the terms of office of the members of the legislative authority should be changed from two to four years

claim: A village council has six members elected at large for four-year terms
quote: composed of six members, who shall be elected by the electors of the village at large, for terms of four years

claim: A statutory city elects a mayor for four years
quote: The mayor of a city shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: A village elects a mayor for four years who presides over council
quote: The mayor of a village shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: A statutory city elects a president of council for two years
quote: the president of the legislative authority of a city shall be elected for a term of two years

claim: A statutory city elects an auditor for four years
quote: The auditor of a city shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: A statutory municipality elects a treasurer for four years
quote: The treasurer of a municipal corporation shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: A statutory city elects a director of law for four years
quote: The city director of law shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: Any municipality, city or village, may adopt a charter
quote: Any municipality may frame and adopt or amend a charter for its government

claim: Municipalities have all powers of local self-government, subject only to the voter-qualification rule of Article V, § 1
quote: Subject to the requirements of Section 1 of Article V of this constitution, municipalities shall have authority to exercise all powers of local self-government

claim: The Cleveland Metropolitan School District board is appointed by the mayor of Cleveland
citation: R.C. 3311.71; City of Cleveland, CMSD Board of Education Appointment Information
quote: Under Ohio law, nine members of the Board of Education of the Cleveland Metropolitan School District are appointed by the Mayor of the City of Cleveland.

claim: Each county elects a prosecuting attorney, auditor, treasurer, clerk of the court of common pleas, sheriff, recorder, engineer and coroner alongside the commissioners
quote: If a vacancy in the office of county commissioner, prosecuting attorney, county auditor, county treasurer, clerk of the court of common pleas, sheriff, county recorder, county engineer, or coroner occurs

claim: Each township elects a fiscal officer alongside its trustees, nominated by petition
quote: The nominating petitions of nonpartisan candidates for township trustee and township fiscal officer

claim: The transition between city and village is regulated by law (the census-driven rule), so a place does not keep its class as it grows or shrinks
quote: The method of transition from one class to the other shall be regulated by law.

claim: Additional (optional) forms of municipal government apply only where a municipality's voters adopt them
quote: no such additional law shall become operative in any municipality until it shall have been submitted to the electors thereof
